intro: Cobblemon Oblivion runs Cobblemon 1.8.1 with Mega Showdown 1.2.0 and more than a hundred community addon packs merged into one server pack. The packs were never made to work together, so a lot was fixed, cut, renamed and rebalanced to make them play nicely. This page lists everything that differs from installing the packs yourself: the big rules first, then pack by pack.

highlights.d: All 1,025 official Pokémon plus 1,465 custom ones from the addon packs, in a single National Pokédex tab. Every custom Pokémon has its own model.
Every Mega has a Mega Stone you can get (most are crafted, and the wiki shows the recipe), except Mega Rayquaza, which Mega Evolves by knowing Dragon Ascent. One Mega per side per battle.

highlights.t: Every move a Pokémon should know
highlights.d: Learnsets are combined across all packs, so no pack's moves get lost. 868 TMs, including 521 new ones for custom moves, crafted with type gems.

highlights.t: Evolutions that work in Adventure mode
highlights.d: Every evolution uses an item a shop can sell and a place that exists in Roria. The packs' own items are back wherever they're harmless (the PokéMarts sell them, and they're used up on evolution); only items that can't exist or are too strong on their own were swapped.
The map's missing blocks are back after the move to the new Minecraft version, and its 225 routes have real encounter tables (3,099 encounters), including fishing spots.
Event Pokémon are only given out at events. Glitch Pokémon hide in a 1-in-2,000 slot on most routes. Fossils can turn up in routes, like Pokémon GO, but never commonly.
One starter screen with 19 regions, from Kanto to Paldea and the fakemon regions.
A full Pokédex with 3D models and shinies, where to find each Pokémon, Mega Stone recipes, a team builder and a route planner.

items.t: The in-game Pokédex has one National tab instead of 60+ regional and pack tabs. It lists exactly the Pokémon the wiki lists (2,490), with regional and pack forms folded into their species' entry.
Like in Cobblemon itself, the Pokédex only lists a form once you have seen it.

Forms have the same names in the Pokédex and on the wiki. A species' default form shows its real name where it has one (e.g. "Shield Forme", "Incarnate Forme", "Red Striped") instead of "Normal", and Megas read like Cobblemon's own ("Mega Charizard Z", "Clone Mega Venusaur", "Hisuian Mega Beedrill").

46 custom "Pokémon" that were really variants of an existing Pokémon became forms of it (e.g. Caos Nincada, Infected Caterpie, Rey Dragonite, Yeti Snorlax), so they share its Pokédex entry. Their evolutions and spawns follow.
74 custom Pokémon are hidden from the Pokédex because they have no model of their own (they would be invisible or a placeholder). Their data is kept, so they come back if a model is ever added.

Over 90 Pokémon names that were lowercase or internal ids (e.g. "amogite", "GreenGorilla", "krab_lyoko") now show proper names, and about 150 forms that showed a raw text key instead of a Pokédex description now show their species' description.

The starter screen shows every region at once, 19 categories: Kanto, Johto, Hoenn, Sinnoh, Unova, Kalos, Alola, Galar, Paldea, Hisui Bias, Special (Pikachu and Eevee), Alatia, Aster, Craftia, Gen 10, Lumora, Northala, Sanrosa and Stick and Apple. Before, packs overwrote each other's lists and only four regions appeared.
Pokédex numbers after the official 1,025 are grouped by pack: each pack gets one block, starters first, then families, Ultra Beasts, paradox, legendary and mythical Pokémon.
Two Drakoons and two Dodiwis are genuinely different Pokémon from different packs that happen to share a name.
Only one Pokémon per side can Mega Evolve per battle. Battle Bond (Ash-Greninja) is not a Mega and doesn't use it up.

Every Mega and Primal totals exactly 100 more base stats than the form it Mega Evolves from, as in the main games. 40 pack Megas were off (Mega Skitty was +240, Mega Mew X +180, Hisuian Mega Slowking +200, Mega Crobat and Hisuian Mega Altaria +0) and were rescaled, keeping each Mega's own shape. Mega Zygarde follows the rule too (808, not the official 778). The one exception is Ultra Necrozma (+154).

Where several packs gave the same Pokémon a Mega, the Megas with genuinely different models all stay, on separate slots: one keeps the plain "Mega" name and the others get a letter (Mega-X, Mega-Y, Mega-Z, Mega-A, Mega-B, Mega-E, Mega-L). All nine slots can be selected. Flygon, for example, has six different Megas from six packs.

Megas with no art of their own were removed with their stones, so no one crafts a stone that does nothing visible (e.g. the pack-invented Mega Rapidash and Mega Mr. Mime). Exact duplicates of another pack's Mega were cut too.

Every Mega Stone can be obtained: 323 stones in total, most crafted from a Mega Stone and a type gem, with each recipe shown on the wiki. 13 stones that had no way to be obtained got a recipe, and recipes for items that don't exist were removed.

Stones that shared a name now have distinct ones: the plain Mega keeps the name and lettered Megas take the letter (Flygonite, Flygonite A / B / Z; Noivernite X / Y / Z). Filename-like names such as 'Porygonitez' were fixed. Stones already in inventories keep working.

Some stones serve several Megas on purpose, and the Pokémon's own form decides the result: Galarian vs Hisuian Slowking, Sableye's Mega-Hisuian, Sandslash's Mega-Alolan, Golurk's copper stages, male/female Meowstic. Greninja's three stones (Ash Greninjite, Greninjite Z, Greninjite) all trigger its Mega; which one you get (Ash, Bond or plain) depends on the Greninja.

Mega Rayquaza needs no stone: it Mega Evolves by knowing Dragon Ascent. Primal Groudon and Kyogre revert in battle while holding the Red Orb or Blue Orb; Primal Dialga does the same with Lost Lore's Time Gear.
Dozens of Megas that looked like the un-evolved Pokémon, wore another pack's Mega model, or couldn't be triggered at all now show their own model and work.

Learnsets are combined across all packs: a Pokémon learns every move any pack gives it. Before, only one pack's list survived, which locked out about 2,100 moves on 827 species. Regional forms' own learnsets apply too.

868 TMs: 296 for official moves that had none (All the Moves), plus 521 for custom pack moves, craftable with the move's type gem (more gems for stronger moves). Any Pokémon that learns one of those moves by level, egg or tutor can also learn it by TM.
78 misspelled moves in pack learnsets (e.g. 'boyslam' for Body Slam) were pointed at the real moves, and 50 custom moves that packs referenced but never defined now exist and work in battle.
Over 400 official moves are rebalanced by the addon packs, so their numbers differ from Bulbapedia on purpose. Where packs disagree, the Pokémon Champions balance values win.
Laser's Additions changes the abilities of 377 official Pokémon on purpose (e.g. Palkia's Pressure becomes Gravity Well). This is kept.
A TM Shop sells every TM, a page per type.

A Move Tutor teaches the special moves a Pokémon can't learn by leveling up, for CobbleDollars (1,500 to 5,000 depending on the move; you only pay when the move is learned). Moves sold as TMs aren't offered, so TMs stay worth buying.

The server is played in Adventure mode with items from shops and rewards, and the reachable places are Roria, the Nether, the End, the Aether and the Twilight Forest. Every evolution was checked, and the ones that needed vanilla blocks and items, items from mods that aren't installed, or biomes and structures that don't exist were switched to Cobblemon items a shop can sell and places you can reach. Each pack's section below lists its own changes.
When several evolutions of one Pokémon used the same item, only the first ever happened. They now use different items. (Level-up evolutions that qualify at the same time let you choose.)
Requirements that packs had misspelled (so the game ignored them) now work: levels, friendship, time of day, weather, biomes and held items.
Evolutions that led to Pokémon or forms that don't exist were removed, and packs' competing evolutions for the same Pokémon were settled.

Some purely cosmetic variant evolutions still use vanilla items that shops sell: Torterra saplings, Meganium flowers, Vivillon honeycomb, Miltank mushrooms, mochi flavours, Skitty wool, candles and the amethyst Layoran. Twilight Forest's Transformation Powder is also used.

Event Pokémon are only given out at events: they don't spawn in the wild, aren't in route tables, and normal Pokémon can't evolve into them (e.g. Eevee into Syn. Eevee or Mikueon, Magikarp into Musclekarp). Each pack's section lists which of its Pokémon are event-only.

Glitch Pokémon (MissingNo., DISABLED, Bad Egg and friends) are extremely rare: most walking routes have one special Glitch slot at about 1 encounter in 2,000, and their natural wild spawns are ultra-rare. They never take a normal route slot.

A few normal Pokémon can still evolve into glitch Pokémon, on purpose: Jigglypuff → DISABLED, Solrock or Lunatone → Galactimon, Pichu → Pinkachu, Dratini → Ryu, Poliwhirl → Poli, Eevee → EEeEE, Paras → Amanita, Kirlia → Charon, Haunter → Nightmare.

Fossil Pokémon can turn up in routes, like Pokémon GO: at most one fossil per route, never more common than Rare. Right now: Mirecanth (Rosecove Island fishing), Scuta (Rosecove Island, Route 7 Lumber Mill), Anobuto (Route 1 Lower, Route 5 Main 2), Raptick (Route 2 Upper 2), Polporos (Route 5 Cave) and Tirtonidos (Route 7 fishing).
Labels were cleaned up across every pack (legendary, mythical, paradox, starter, fossil, event, glitch), which decides what can appear in routes. The pack sections list the changes.

Blocks lost when the map moved to the new Minecraft version were restored: Anthian City (about 70,000 black sandstone blocks) and other areas that had turned to air are back, with palm, baobab, willow, maple and cherry trees, torches, ladders, signs and banners. About 78,000 blocks in total.
Old Pixelmon healers and PC were replaced with Cobblemon Healing Machines and a PC in the same spots.
Location titles now show only to the player who walks in, not to everyone on the server.

All 225 zones have encounter tables (3,099 encounters, counting the seasonal and lunar ones). Every Pokémon that isn't legendary, mythical, paradox, an Ultra Beast or event-only can be caught somewhere from the start, starters and every regional or alternate wild form included. Evolved Pokémon are rarer and appear at levels near where they would evolve. Rarities are Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare (and Glitch). Legendaries, mythicals and paradoxes come from raid dens, Ultra Beasts from Ultra Wormholes.
The 15 fishing spots never actually worked with a fishing rod. They now do, and only water Pokémon bite there.

Routes change with the seasons: each route has an extra Pokémon for spring, summer, autumn and winter, and Spring Espeon, Summer Glaceon, Autumn Sylveon, Winter Jolteon and Winter Petilil and Lilligant only appear in their season.

Lunar events are rare, roughly once every five hours of play. During a Blood, Blue, Harvest or Super Moon each route has an extra themed Pokémon, and Blood Moon Umbreon, Bloodmoon Milotic and Sableye, Blue Moon Flareon and Harvest Moon Leafeon only appear then.
Only first-stage Pokémon live in the wild, each in one zone: the earliest one near its level. Evolve them yourself; PokéMarts sell the evolution items.

Fish-like Pokémon (Magikarp, Goldeen, Chinchou, Horsea, Feebas, Wailmer and about 65 more families) can only be caught with a fishing rod, and everything else only on foot. Each fishing spot has at least 3 Pokémon, so a fish may bite in up to 3 spots.
114 forms that could not be caught before (like Infected and Coterian Caterpie) now each have a zone.
Every town has a PokéMart. Shops sell more the further the town is in the story: Poké Balls, medicine, Repels, X items and evolution items.
The Battle Tower opens once you beat the Champions.

The new Pokémon from the October packs (Catrmons, Dunadex, Toon's Mons, SpaceworldMons, Kettlephant and Phantea, Potle, Dissonitten, Prodifry, Virosis) and the new wild forms (Dawnian Meowth, Treecko, Torchic, Mudkip and more, and Smog, Sound, Jack and Vision Rotom) each have a zone.

Radical Cobblemon Trainers' NPC trainers that use alternate forms (Therian Landorus, Origin Giratina, Crowned Zacian...) spawn correctly. A few want forms no pack here has (Sevii regional forms, Surfing Pikachu...) and use the normal form.
Because Laser's Additions changes the abilities of 377 official Pokémon, some trainers' Pokémon have Laser's abilities instead of the ones the trainer's author picked.

Every Roria trainer has a skin: one per trainer class (male and female versions for Ace Trainers, Swimmers, Pirates and Eclipse Grunts) and their own for the gym leaders, Elite Four, Champions, rivals and other special trainers.

About 80 models asked for animations that don't exist, which could crash the game when they were drawn (in the Pokédex, in battle or in the wild). All repaired; where no animation exists, the Pokémon simply stands still in that pose.

Pack files that overwrote each other were separated: Pokémon wearing another pack's texture, Megas drawn with another pack's body, Minior losing its meteor form, Roggenrola's line losing its looks, and 51 packs' changes to Pokémon that were silently dropped because two packs used the same file name (e.g. Hisuian Kakuna, Nandian Dugtrio, Gigantamax Electrode).
Pokédex pictures that were invisible, off-frame or showed the plain form were fixed, and Cobblemon's own region-bias looks (e.g. Pikachu's blue eyes) are switched on.
A player Pokédex for this exact server: every Pokémon with its forms, stats, abilities, moves and evolutions, and a 3D model viewer with a shiny toggle. Each form shows which pack it comes from.
"Where to find it" on every Pokémon's page lists the routes it appears in, and the Zones tab shows every route's table.
Mega Stones show their crafting recipe, and the item list covers every held item, Mega Stone and Z-Crystal.

A Team Builder with legal moves, abilities, items, IVs and EVs, plus a team suggester that builds teams for any level the way the main games build trainers: route trainers with low IVs and EVs and their latest level-up moves, gym leaders and champions with stronger builds.

known: CobbleZones' "have you caught it" check (in the zone encounter view and PokeNav maps) errors when opened. Zones, spawns and zone battles all work.
Several hundred custom Pokémon still have no Pokédex description text.
Some models have no animation for every pose and stand still in those.
Caramouse, Cinnamouse and Nautilord list an ability (Screen Cleaner, Heavy Metal) in their learnset by mistake; those entries do nothing.

notes.t: Packs that re-declared official forms (Minior Meteor, Ash-Greninja, and regional Vulpix, Ninetales, Ponyta, Rapidash, Voltorb, Lilligant and Exeggutor) created duplicate copies that could never appear; the duplicates were removed and the packs' art still applies to the official forms (17 in total).
Built on Cobblemon 1.8.1.
Region-bias forms (Pokémon that will evolve into a regional form) are now labelled with the region's name, e.g. "Alolan" or "Galarian", instead of "Alola-Bias".

Cobblemon's built-in region-bias look pack, normally switched off, is now always on: region-bias Pokémon get their visual differences, such as Pikachu's blue eyes, Cubone, Koffing, Pichu, Exeggcute, Mime Jr. and the Hisui-bias starters (16 species).
Plain Vivillon is now labelled "Meadow Pattern", and the duplicate Meadow form was hidden.
Genesect's Drive forms now show their art.
Basculin's default form is labelled "Red Striped".
Greninja's Mega of the Bond form is labelled "Mega Bond Greninja".
Arceus plates, Silvally memories, Genesect drives, Ogerpon masks and Origin forms come from the held item, so the team suggester gives them that item.
Dipplin → Hydrapple: the Dragon's Breath alternative was removed; learning Dragon Cheer (Cobblemon's own route) stays.
Cobblemon's own quirks are left as they are: Pikachu caps and Vivillon's biome-based patterns.

The Pokédex wiki now shows the Megas and Gigantamax forms that come from Mega Showdown itself (33 species such as Mega Raichu X and Y, Starmie, Dragonite, Meganium, Greninja, Froslass, Meowstic, Excadrill, Malamar, Pyroar, Drampa, Eelektross, Scolipede, Emboar, Chesnaught, Barbaracle and Glimmora). These always worked in game; only the wiki was missing them.
Iron Mothite and Roaring Moonite did nothing when held; they now work.
Mega Rayquaza has no stone on purpose: it Mega Evolves by knowing Dragon Ascent.
Built on Mega Showdown 1.2.0, which adds Absol Mega-Z, Mega Baxcalibur, Garchomp Mega-Z, Mega Golisopod, and Lucario Mega-Z.
Partner Cap Pikachu showed the plain Pikachu model in the Pokédex; it now shows the cap.
Mega Meowstic uses one model and texture for both genders; that is how Mega Showdown ships it.
Alolan Gogoat's animations were linked under a misspelled name and now play.
All the Moves adds 296 TMs for official moves that had none.
Altered Pokemon's own Mega Flygon, Mega Gallade and Mega Gardevoir were dropped because Altered Pokemon Additions ships the same Megas; both Altered packs are otherwise kept.

Altered Pokemon's Altered Mega Gardevoir file was overwriting Mega Showdown's, leaving regular Mega Gardevoir with no model; both now load. The same fix restored models for Mega Gallade and Mega Metagross.
Where both Altered packs define the same form, the Altered Pokemon Additions version wins: Espeon's Altered form keeps Solar Flare and Gardevoir's Altered Mega keeps Burning Soul.
Its Gallade and Gardevoir Mega Stones did nothing when held; they now work.

The Nether Star alternatives for Altered A Eevee → Altered Umbreon and Altered B Eevee → Altered Espeon were removed; the level-up routes (friendship, midnight, Moon Stone / friendship, noon, Sun Stone) stay.
Kabutops could never take its Alterform Steel form (unlike Kabuto); it now can.
Alterform Fire Beedrill was missing from the game (its file clashed with another pack's) and is now back.
Amogite and Prolongus were missing their models because the pack's resource half was absent; it was added, so both now render and stay in the Pokédex.
amogite and prolongus are now capitalised as Amogite and Prolongus.
Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): Amogite, Prolongus.

Nandian Dugtrio was missing from the game entirely (its file was silently overwritten by another with the same name) and is now back. Nandian Diglett and Dugtrio also no longer randomly show the plain model.
Included in full: remodels, spawns, drops and recipes built for Mega Showdown. It replaces some official art on purpose, including Entei, Heatran, Aegislash and Arceus, plus four cries.
ATM x MSD's Frosmoth remodel was dropped in favour of Snom Betterified's Snom/Frosmoth pair.
Hisuian Growlithe's model asked for animations no pack provides; fixed so it no longer risks a crash.
Easter egg: Alolan Unown is an Unown T with a QR code. It can now actually be obtained as the Alolan form, and its QR code is shown all the time, not just in battle as the pack originally did.
Temga is now labelled legendary and Creslume mythical (kept out of routes).

Regiclay → Registeel, Regirock and Regice (traded while holding the matching item) now really check the pack's extra conditions, which were being ignored: thunderstorm for Registeel, clear weather for Regirock, level 50 for Regice.

Regiclay can evolve into 10 more Regis by being traded while holding an item: Magnet → Regieleki, Dragon Fang → Regidrago, Twisted Spoon → Reginigma, Black Glasses → Regitenebris, Miracle Seed → Regimoss, Mystic Water → Regihydro, Absorb Bulb → Regiplenti, Reaper Cloth → Regisculk, Silk Scarf → Regifurr, Silver Powder → Regisecto.
Karfoal → Keldeo now requires holding a Black Belt (was a Diamond Sword written in a way the game couldn't read).
Haidon → Koraidon and Kaidon → Miraidon now use an Open-Faced Sandwich (was a Farmer's Delight chicken sandwich; that mod isn't installed).
Todlbug was shipped by more than one pack; Big and Small's version is the one kept.
Big and Small's Bovittle is the one kept; Grow and Gather Reborn's identical copy was removed.
Pokorb's Roseate form now trades into Voltorb like its five sibling colour forms, instead of into nothing.

Big and Small stays on 1.0.1 (1.1.0 is Fabric-only and would break six existing evolutions), but 8 new species from 1.1.0 were added: Feathortle, Kadazzle, Onizz, Pichungus, Salamagma, Toadress, Trenchlax and Unowin. Kilindra was not added (needs a mod-only item).
Trenchlax's addition no longer replaces Munchlax's drops with a jelly bean item that doesn't exist, and Salamagma learns Lava Plume (its misspelled move pointed at nothing).
Ditrans can now learn Waterfall and Fly from tutors (the entries were misspelled).
Unowin's default form is labelled "A".
Salamagma's pre-evolution is now Charmeleon, matching how it actually evolves.
Porygon2 → Poranger: the held Nether Star is now used up; the Netherite Upgrade alternative was removed.
Farfetch'd → Baguetch'd: the held Bread is now used up.
Bovittle → Red and Brown Mooshtank Miltank now happen in a swamp (Roria has no Mushroom Fields).
Bovittle → Bouffalant now happens in plains instead of a village (Roria has no villages).
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Blue-Eyes.
The Pokémon Champions balance pack was added: 41 move rebalances, 3 ability changes and 2 status-condition changes to official moves (e.g. Absorb 20→40 power, Anchor Shot 80→90, Bloodmoon 140→130).

Where other packs also rebalanced the same moves, Champions' values now win (e.g. Slash stays 80 power Normal instead of Craftiamon's 70 Steel; Psyshield Bash 90 power/90 acc instead of Laser's 70/100). 102 competing definitions were retired so each move has exactly one version.
Champions pack updated: adds learnsets for 195 official Pokémon, an Eject Button held-item change and a Run Away change; regional-form learnsets are kept.
Adds 308 new moves to official Pokémon learnsets on top of their normal movepools (nothing is taken away).
Kommo-o's Champions learnset was never being applied because of a misspelled name; it now applies.
Gardevoir's Twiloud form was declared twice; the duplicate was removed.
Iron Soom and Iron Spnd (paradox Latias/Latios) were removed; they shipped with plain Latias/Latios Pokédex entries pasted in.
Iron Torpedo, Wild Burning and Rough Byte were renamed (display names corrected).
Removed a stray blue-dye evolution from Riolu; the real route is Lucario → Cariolus.
Shiny Iron Blawing had no texture because of a stray space in its file name; the shiny now shows.
The Twiloud starter category was removed from the starter screen; its Pokémon remain in the game.
Iron Care is now labelled a paradox Pokémon (kept out of routes).
Its gem Diancie Mega is hidden: it is identical to another Diancie form.
Gigantamax Electrode was missing from the game (its file clashed with another pack's) and is now back.
CobbleMega+ adds Mega Nidoking with its own model and a craftable Nidokingite. The pack was repaired so the stone works in battle and has a proper name.
Glownet shipped with no base stats and no moves; it now has 460 total stats (matching its Red and Green Light forms) and its pre-evolution Bulbee's 42 moves.
Rondidi's model asked for a missing running animation; fixed so it no longer risks a crash.
Glownet had no abilities of its own (only its forms did), which caused errors; the species now has abilities.
Ballearia has separate Male and Female forms in the Pokédex, so the gender button shows the right model. Wild gender is still rolled normally.
Eevee → Prismeon keeps the Shiny Stone and now works reliably (EEeEE no longer competes for it).
New evolution: Eevee → Glideon by levelling up while holding a Float Stone. Glideon's data named Eevee as its pre-evolution, but nothing evolved into it.
Sonayre → Ballearia: a broken duplicate female-only evolution was removed; the normal level 35 evolution gives a female Ballearia when Sonayre is female.
Revendier → Stouthound, Burstile → Nitragon, Choirtoise → Turalyzer and Tikishock → Ursashock now require their intended level as well as friendship (the level was being ignored).
New evolution: a female Yellow Light Glownet evolves into Beaquin at level 36 (like Combee → Vespiquen). Beaquin's data named it as the pre-evolution but the pack never added the evolution.
Now classed as fossil Pokémon (at most one per route, Rare or rarer): Leemaura, Crinaurus, Tirtonidos, Ramcosta, Pawleo, Blazera, Divera, Glidera, Oozera, Anobuto, Kabumaldo, Shieldanyte, Omastiodon.
Fixed a game crash when Chameleos was drawn (for example in the Pokédex).
Brachydios and Chameleos were invisible in the Pokédex picture; both now show properly. Lunagaron's picture was fixed the same way.
Chameleos' big Pokédex picture showed its invisible camouflage pose; it now shows the full body.
Chameleos turning invisible in the world outside of battle is intentional: it is its camouflage, as its Pokédex text says.

Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Whelp, Gigginox, Khezu, Rathling, Rathalos, Rathian, Malfestio, Deviljho, Brachydios, Ahtal-Ka, Ahtal-Neset, Palico, Duramboros, Uragaan, Chameleos, Odogaron, Palamute, Gypceros, Zinogre, Rachnoid, Nerscylla, Rakna-kadaki, Bazelgeuse, Tetsy, Tetsucabra, Lunagaron.

Seven seasonal and lunar Eeveelution looks are real forms now, listed in the Pokédex: Spring Espeon, Summer Glaceon, Autumn Sylveon, Winter Jolteon, Blood Moon Umbreon, Blue Moon Flareon and Harvest Moon Leafeon.

Eevee reaches Summer Glaceon, Winter Jolteon, Blue Moon Flareon and Harvest Moon Leafeon by levelling up while holding the stone (Ice, Thunder, Fire, Leaf) in that season or during the Super Moon. Using the stone always gives the normal form.
Marowak → Skelaymore now uses a Razor Claw (was a Netherite Sword).
Cobblemon Void added: Sedimite and its three evolutions Sedimage, Sedimonk and Sedruid, with full models and 3 signature moves. Its unused 'Cosmic' type was left out.
Cobblepastas' Unown King was removed in favour of Pastamon's Psychic/Dark Unown King.
Freakachu was removed from the dex.
Learow ships without any animation file; it no longer risks crashing the game and simply stands still in those poses.
Pinkachu no longer shows a placeholder model.
Eerie Ditto's texture was painted for Cobblemon's old Ditto model; it has been recoloured onto the current model (eerie greys, and eerie greens when shiny).

Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): Glitchlett, DISABLED, Poli, Amanita, Learow, FUtiLE, Pinkachu, Ryu, Charon, Nightmare, Ghost, EEeEE, 731, Galactimon, X32763, Faceleech, Turmur, Mishanter, Bad Egg, Manafetus, S♪REN. Manafetus and S♪REN are no longer labelled legendary.
Cofawer is no longer labelled legendary.
Eevee → EEeEE now uses a Dubious Disc. It used the Shiny Stone, which Prismeon also uses, so only one of the two could ever happen.
Poliwhirl → Poli now uses a Razor Claw (was an Iron Sword).
Pichu → Pinkachu: the held Pink Concrete is now used up.

The glitch evolutions stay: Jigglypuff → DISABLED, Solrock or Lunatone → Galactimon, Pichu → Pinkachu, Dratini → Ryu, Poliwhirl → Poli, Eevee → EEeEE, Paras → Amanita, Kirlia → Charon, Haunter → Nightmare.
8 CobbleStar entries that only had a shared placeholder model are hidden from the Pokédex, plus Blackbelt and Monica at the server owner's request.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): F-00.
Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): Bellelba. It is no longer labelled paradox.

Wardevoir (Dark/Fairy) and its Mega Evolution (Dark/Fighting, Wardevoirite, crafted with a Dark Gem), plus Regiate (Steel/Fire, labelled legendary like the other Regis). Only these three were taken from Cobbleworks: none of its other Pokémon, plushies, coins or accessories.
Regiate dropped Andesite Casing from the Create mod, which isn't installed; it drops iron ingots instead.
Neither has natural spawns: where they appear is up to the server's routes and events.
Coterian Piplup, Chespin, Quilladin and Chesnaught are hidden: the pack ships no art for them.
Pichu → Coterian Pikachu now checks its biome, and Coterian Caterpie → Metapod and Coterian Metapod → Butterfree now check their level (these were being ignored).
Craftiamon's Slash rebalance (70 power, Steel) is overridden by the Champions version.
Stray, Creeping and Dolittle are now labelled starters (kept out of routes). Elderian is no longer labelled mythical.
Garudian → Elderian now happens in a deep ocean (was a cold ocean; Roria's sea is deep ocean), and the held Heart of the Sea is used up.
Wallopett and Xanatu were drawn above the frame of the Pokédex picture (so looked invisible); they are now framed correctly.
Only Mega Mew and Mega Ceruledge are taken from Cusmega; its Latias, Greninja, Rayveltal and Rizkrozma and its duplicate Ceruledge were left out.
Mega Mew and Mega Ceruledge are added as Mega-X forms of Mew and Ceruledge, with new stones (Mewnite X, Ceruledgite X) since the pack shipped none.
New pack: Sting (Bug/Poison, 445 base stat total).
Kevin (Ice/Fire, 716 base stat total) was left out at the owner's request.
Sting's shiny texture was painted for a different version of its model and looked broken; it was redrawn from the normal texture with pale blue accents.
Sting's misspelled "Poisonsting" move is now Poison Sting, learned at level 35.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Sting.
MissingNo was shipped by more than one pack; Errormons' MissingNo is the one kept.
MissingNo's variants are now forms of MissingNo: Ghost, Aerodactyl, Kabutops and Saturation.
Form-to-base evolutions (e.g. Ghost Missingno back to Missingno) are kept as part of the pack's mechanics; the same applies to Solrock's Deactivated and Lunatone's New Moon/Half Moon forms.
Fixed a game crash when scrolling the Pokédex past MissingNo, caused by a broken animation link. The same kind of problem could crash the game in battles or wild encounters too.
MissingNo's four forms now show their own art.
Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): MissingNo., >A, ゥL ||ゥM 4, A, ◣ゥ 8, ゥ .4, H POKé, 'Ng ゥ$, ゥ.
Eevee → Minereon now requires holding a Hard Stone in any cave (was an Iron Pickaxe in Dripstone Caves, which Roria doesn't have).
Eevee → Dungeon now happens in any cave (was the Deep Dark, which Roria doesn't have); it still needs a held Lantern.
Primal Shell and Saber Jaw are now labelled paradox Pokémon (kept out of routes).

10 new Pokémon: Bloodsplitter, Chrysopierce, Faylure, Harpivoir, Lootoad, Luminimp, Magipole, Scryu, Selyn (legendary) and Thaumatoad, plus Bloodmoon Milotic and Sableye, Blossom Phantump and Trevenant, Draconic Tinkaton, and Libra Unown, the first of the Zodiac Unown (its Celestial ability doubles its stats). They bring 13 new abilities, 11 new moves and two new weathers, Blood Moon and Blue Moon.

Evolutions use items the server can sell. Bloodmoon Milotic and Sableye, Bloodsplitter (from Ariados) and Faylure (from Blossom Phantump): level up at night holding a Dusk Stone, instead of the mod's Bloodstone. Harpivoir: use a Dusk Stone on Gardevoir at night with high friendship, instead of the Harpy Lyre. Chrysopierce: use a Sun Stone on Charcadet, because its Dawn Stone already evolves Charcadet into Tekioledge.

Only the Pokémon were taken. The mod's items (gemstones, Bloodstone, Myth Ball, Harpy Feather and Lyre), the Moon Temple, the blood moon event, its Lunatone rebalance and its Pokémon interactions are not included.
None of them has natural spawns: where they appear is up to the server's routes and events.
Rey Dragonite is now a "Rey" form of Dragonite.

Mega Pawmot and Mega Lokdana are now real Mega forms of Pawmot and Lokdana, reached with new Mega Stones (Pawmotite, Lokdanite), instead of separate Pokémon. Their bogus level-50 evolutions into the Mega were removed.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Hollowknight.
Solrock and Lunatone's "Complete" forms are now drawn in the Pokédex.
Monolith Nosepass and Probopass showed a see-through body with a floating nose in the Pokédex; they now show their colours.
Brewcargo had no abilities of its own (only its potion forms did); it now has Curious Medicine and hidden ability Power of Alchemy, the two its forms share.
Bludgymph → Smitefae now uses a Max Revive (was a Totem of Undying).

Woohorn evolves from Leug, as intended: trade Leug while it holds a Leaf Stone, or level it up in a taiga while it holds a Leaf Stone (it learns Horn Leech). The pack had put these routes on Karrablast by mistake, and Leug's own level 35 evolution pointed at a Woohorn form that doesn't exist.
Karrablast no longer evolves into Woohorn; its other evolutions are unchanged.
Adds six new flower colours as forms of Flabébé, Floette and Florges.

Frostbound adds Frostbound forms of Sprigatito and Floragato (Grass/Dragon) and Meowscarada (Fairy/Dragon, 530 total stats), with new abilities Dragon Veil and Mystical Floral (Grass moves become Dragon/Fairy and +20%).
Frostbound forms are permanent (not battle-only), Floragato's form now animates, and they don't conflict with Paldea Starter Megas' Mega Meowscarada.
Frostbound forms have no natural spawns; they are placed through zones.
Now classed as fossil Pokémon (at most one per route, Rare or rarer): Arctoplesio, Dracocerato, Dunkleovish, Raptorzolt.
The wild spawns of Browt, Pombon, Gecqua, Mr. Windychu and Mrs. Wavychu were being silently ignored because of badly named files; they now load.
Browt, Pombon and Gecqua get their own "Gen 10" starter category.
Desmotel's and Isuckle's egg moves now work (the entries were misspelled).
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Goom, Googaloo, Googaloothwomp, Reita.
Omnicog's routes using items from the Create mod, which isn't installed, were removed.
Only five Gigantamax models are used: Garbodor, Orbeetle, Drednaw, Coalossal and Flapple. Kingler, Lapras, Inteleon, Appletun and Centiskorch keep Mega Showdown's Gigantamax models.
Horret's Mega Ceruledge keeps the plain "Mega" name; Cusmega's becomes Mega-X.
Rowlet and Decidueye animations from this pack no longer overwrite Cobblemon's own (21 such animation clashes across packs were separated).
Mega Decidueye is back (it was dropped in newer versions of the pack). Its stone, Deciduite, is made at a smithing table from a Miracle Seed, a Mega Stone and a Ghost Gem.

Its variants are now forms of the official Pokémon: Lanturn (Kullat), Sneasel (Dreadful Claw), Dusknoir (Tesla), Electivire (Raijin), Magmortar (Eternal Forge), Golurk (Gear Guardian), Scolipede (War Mount) and Golisopod (Fallen Ronin).
Lediboltdef was hidden from the Pokédex at the server owner's request.
Highyena's pre-evolution is now Mightyena, matching how it actually evolves.
Crabominable → Crabbuki now happens on Jagged Peaks (Roria has no glacier biome).
Mightyena → Highyena's party requirement was cleaned up so it reads correctly.

Hacnealit is now the "Lit" form of Hacnea rather than a separate Pokémon: give Hacnea a candle to light it, level it up to turn it back. Lit Hacnea evolves into Jacturne at level 24. One Pokédex entry instead of two.
Hacnea no longer shows a placeholder model, and its "Lit" form is now drawn in the Pokédex (it needed a carved face).
Its five scarf starters are now a "Scarf" form of Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander, Squirtle and Eevee instead of separate Pokémon.

Scarf forms are now purely cosmetic: they had the fully evolved Pokémon's stats (a scarf Pikachu out-stat a normal one); they now have exactly the same stats, moves and abilities as the normal Pokémon.

Scarf Charmander showed as pink and black because it used Cobblemon's old tail-flame textures; fixed. 22 similar broken texture layers in other packs were removed, and 15 missing shiny or sleeping textures now fall back to the normal look.
Gimmighoul → Golemarche now works anywhere (was inside Trial Chambers, which Roria doesn't have); it still needs a held Compass.
Oakabaa, Moocoal and Oinkelp get their own "Stick and Apple" starter category.
Now classed as fossil Pokémon (at most one per route, Rare or rarer): Sparkle, Soarave, Sparvyrn.

Laser's Additions deliberately changes abilities on official Pokémon: 85 Pokémon gain an extra ability (e.g. Abomasnow gains Snow Force) and 294 have one ability swapped for a new one (e.g. Palkia's Pressure becomes Gravity Well, Dialga's becomes Stasis Armor). These swaps are kept as the pack intended.
Laser's Additions' Absol Mega was dropped as a duplicate, leaving ZA Mega's Absol Mega-Z uncontested.
Pillowisp no longer evolves into Phantasmare's removed 'Bad Dreams' form.
Laser's Psyshield Bash rebalance (70 power, 100 accuracy) is overridden by the Champions version.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Shade.
Sephiredge, Obyless and Shade are now labelled mythical (kept out of routes); Shade is also event-only.
Ender Clamperl → Boxtail: the Shulker Shell alternative was removed; the Box Shell route stays.
Ender Clamperl → Elabyss: a broken alternative using an item that doesn't exist was removed; the Telepearl route stays.
Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): Suslett, Sustrio.
The whole Caos set is now "Caos" forms of the official Pokémon: Nincada, Litten, Zigzagoon, Tynamo, Skitty, Finneon, Chingling, Croagunk, Buizel, Hatenna, Snom, Ducklett, Wurmple and Baltoy.
Zyvelta's flying animation asked for a pose that doesn't exist; it now uses its idle animation.
Froling, Tertwag and Ckotox are no longer offered on the starter screen (the Legend category was removed); they remain in the game.
The pack's species are no longer labelled "legend"; Zyvelta is no longer labelled legendary or restricted, and Froling, Tertwag and Ckotox are no longer labelled starters.
LightMons' Eevee 'Starter' form was removed — it was just plain Eevee with another name.
Calybrea, Driby and Gorgoop have the ability Toxic Voice, which the pack never actually defined. It now works as the pack describes: sound-based attacking moves have a 30% chance to poison.
Foliqi's evolution into Yi-gami (Foli-qi form) pointed at a misspelled species and would have failed when it tried to evolve; it now works.
Pachyquag, Diplit and Haiproto are now labelled starters (kept out of routes).
Replaces Celesteela's model and adds an "Aptrumi" variant form; the new model reliably overrides the default.
Literally Just Celesteela changes Celesteela's abilities.

Lively Mons ships its regional forms twice (a "Lively" and a "Sanrosan" copy); the second copy now has a distinguishing suffix in its name. Affects Krookodile, Krokorok, Sandile, Shuckle and Heracross.
Version 1.11.1: includes the 8 species added in 1.11, a Lotad addition and reworked spawns.
Fungalith no longer shows a placeholder model.
Now classed as fossil Pokémon (at most one per route, Rare or rarer): Laprise, Hollorn, Calciopi, Polporos, Spinarift.
Citrillume, Infernito and Potdary are now labelled starters (kept out of routes).
Lost Lore's Clone Mega X Charizard is kept as its own Mega alongside the official Mega Charizard X; it is reached only by a Clone Charizard.
Clone Bulbasaur and Clone Ivysaur had never rendered because they pointed at a model that doesn't exist; they now use the correct model.
Lost Lore's special stones keep their own names: Crystalline Steelixite, Shadow Mewtwonite X and Mewtwonite X (instead of a generic 'Steelixite Y').
Final Option now shows a proper name, and Diamond Drill is Crystal type (Lost Lore's type used by Crystal Onix and Crystal Steelix).
Lost Lore 3.1.0 (the first version that runs on Cobblemon 1.8): adds Mewtwo Mega-Armored, Floette and Greninja additions and the Drone Strike move.
AZ's Floette ('Ange', reached with Lost Lore's Light of Life item) keeps Lost Lore's own 900 base stat total (250/75/200/165/200/10).
The Clone forms (e.g. Clone Mega Venusaur) showed the plain model in the Pokédex; they now show their own models.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): MT, MT2, Black Fog. They are no longer labelled legendary.
Lana Eevee → Lana Sylveon now correctly requires knowing a Fairy-type move (the condition was being ignored).
Crystal Onix → Crystal Steelix now correctly checks its level requirement.

Primal Dialga comes from Lost Lore: hold the craftable Time Gear and Dialga undergoes Primal Reversion when it's sent into battle and reverts afterwards, exactly like Primal Groudon and Kyogre. (Lost Lore made it look Primal whenever it held the Time Gear; it now changes only in battle.)
The Mega and Gigantamax forms of Venuspheal, Charizpheal, Blasphoise and Sphikachu were removed because they had no art of their own and looked like the base Pokémon.
Spharmander now learns Rollout at level 1 (the entry had no learn method).
Bulbaspheal, Spharmander and Spheatle are no longer labelled starters, so they can appear in routes.
Charspheleon's pre-evolution is now Spharmander, matching how it actually evolves.
Lotus Megas' Mega Typhlosion (Typhlonite) could never be triggered; it now works.
Lotus Megas' Typhlosion Mega is now labelled 'Mega-L' instead of being a second form called 'Mega'.
Names fixed: Krab, Megatank, Blok, Kankrelat and Hornet now show proper names instead of internal ones.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Krab, Megatank, Blok, Kankrelat, Hornet. They are no longer labelled Ultra Beasts.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): MechaMew2.
Noivern's Megas: MegaStorm's keeps the plain "Mega" name, Skull's Mega Expansion's becomes Mega-X, Horret's becomes Mega-Y and MuShiro's becomes Mega-Z.
MegaStorm's Walreinite did nothing when held; it now Mega Evolves Walrein.
Mega Typhlosion from MegaStorm's Gen 1 fixes was removed: it duplicated MegaStorm's Mega-Y Typhlosion with the same stats and no art of its own.
Empoleonite can now be crafted (recipe with the type gem).
Included: new Minior models and textures, which also apply to the official Meteor form (the pack's duplicate Meteor form was removed).

Several Vivillon patterns (e.g. High Plains, Icy Snow) were spelled differently from their art and showed the plain look; fixed. About 70 drawn patterns from three Vivillon packs could never actually be rolled; they can now appear.
The rainbow Scatterbug, Spewpa and Vivillon form is labelled "Iridescense".
Spewpa → Columbina, 666 and Poké Ball pattern Vivillon: their time and advancement requirements were misspelled and are now checked.

Cut down to the 9 Mega-E forms with real custom art: Raticate, Torterra, Luxray, Gogoat, Pawmot, Annihilape, Flareon, Espeon and Infernape. The rest (near-identical recolours, and Megas with no art at all) were left out.
Each kept Mega-E has its own Mega Stone: Raticitee, Torterritee, Luxrayitee, Gogoatitee, Pawmitee, Annihilitee, Flareonitee, Espeonitee and Infernitee.
Mega-E Serperior was left out: its texture is just Serperior's own.
The pack's own stone recipes need its code mod, which isn't installed, so they were removed; the Mega-E forms use the stones above instead.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Musclekarp.
Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): Lord Helix.
Magikarp no longer evolves into Musclekarp, since Musclekarp is event-only.

Where MuShiro's Megas competed with another pack's, MuShiro's version keeps the plain "Mega" name and the other pack's Mega moves to a letter (Drifblim, Electivire, Hydreigon, Klinklang, Krookodile, Lilligant).
Mushiro Mega's Mega Skeledirge pose file was repaired so it animates correctly.

31 second Megas (e.g. Mushiro Mega's Haxorus Mega-X and Volcarona Mega-X) that returned after a bug fix are real, distinct models and stay by decision, even when they look closer to the base Pokémon than another pack's Mega.
Mushiro Mega's Luxray Mega-Y has separate male and female art.
Bambud, Bamnon, Pyrilis, Solafae, Yakru and Yakhan are no longer labelled starters, so they can appear in routes.

Mega Meowscarada and Mega Quaquaval added. The pack was completely non-functional as shipped (no names, stones that couldn't register or be crafted, Megas that could never trigger); all repaired, Quaquaval's Mega made battle-only, and base Meowscarada no longer rolled back.
The Iron Moth and Roaring Moon Mega Stones (Ironmothite and Roaring Moonite) were in an outdated format and could not load; they now work.
Ironmothite and Roaring Moonite can now be crafted (recipe with the type gem).
Pastamon's "missingnumber" was removed as a duplicate of Errormons' MissingNo.
Two packs shipped an Unown King; Pastamon's Psychic/Dark Unown King is the one kept.
Lost Pikachu is now a "Lost Lore" form of Pikachu.
Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): White-Hand, Unown-King. Unown-King is also labelled legendary.
Only the Iron Jugulis and Iron Boulder remodels are included; the pack's 14 other remodels, which would have replaced official Cobblemon models, were left out.
Perry was removed from the dex.
Pocket Universal's six fusion "starters" are not on the starter screen.
Venosquirt and Nidowart have separate Male and Female forms in the Pokédex, so the gender button shows the right model. Wild gender is still rolled normally.
Now classed as fossil Pokémon (at most one per route, Rare or rarer): Mirecanth, Raptick, Galiraptor, Galoraptor.
The 18 fusion Pokémon that were labelled starters (e.g. Charbasquir, Bulbashield, Venosquirt, Nidowart) no longer are, so they can appear in routes. Ecliptable is no longer labelled a baby Pokémon.
Grow and Gather Reborn's Bovittle and Todlbug were identical copies of Big and Small's and were removed in favour of those.
Squashologne's default form is labelled "Male".
Chomppest, Choncub, Rockocroco, Tutel, Snowwing, Spirikid, Pudlphant, Moldjinn and Beesilissa are no longer labelled mythical.
Omnigrub only evolves into Ultimagrub (level 100). Its 21 other evolutions into official bugs were removed.

Pokémon Overcharge adds 42 craftable held items: 18 Crayons (add a type to a single-type Pokémon), 18 Erasers (remove one type from a dual-type Pokémon), plus Blank Plate, D20, Old Shield, Polarized Glass, Shocking Orb and Training Wheels.
Its 6 moves and 7 abilities were left out because no Pokémon learns or has them, and its paralysis rule change (1-in-4) and Ear Muffs were dropped in favour of Champions' and Laser's versions.
Celebird's texture no longer falls back to a placeholder.
Porygon-Z's Mega Stone pointed at a removed Mega; it now works.
Qlovean Honchkrow and Qlovean Noctowl could crash the game because of wing animations for bones their models don't have; fixed.
Qlovean Murkrow → Qlovean Honchkrow now uses a Max Revive (was a Totem of Undying).

Rotom's appliance forms used a "Monitor" item that doesn't exist. Rotom now changes form with shop items: Water Stone → Wash, Air Balloon → Fan, Ice Stone → Frost, Fire Stone → Heat, Leaf Stone → Mow, Metal Coat → Push.
Push Rotom returns to plain Rotom with a Cell Battery; the copper bulb and Appliances-mod routes were removed.
Mega Torkoal (Fire/Steel, 570 total stats, battle-only, own model) added with a craftable Torkoalite; nothing else from the pack (it would have replaced Lugia's model).
Scorching Kiln is now labelled a paradox Pokémon (kept out of routes).
Now classed as fossil Pokémon (at most one per route, Rare or rarer): Scuta, Mantiverous.
The pack's Pokémon are now labelled as custom Pokémon (Gorochu, Tumbell, Sproutopod, Feistling, Cassowrath, Tentango, Umamirage, Scuta, Mantiverous).
Shriekumo now correctly evolves into Echolossus, which nothing could reach before.
Removed a stray duplicate evolution on Flarichi (the real one lives on Flareon).
Leaforest and Mimivee no longer show a placeholder model.
Espilevi is now labelled a paradox Pokémon (kept out of routes).
Leafipotent and Vaporipotent are no longer labelled legendary; Clockage, Minadial and Dragash are no longer pseudo-legendary, and Mechabang is labelled Powerhouse instead.
Leafipotent and Vaporipotent were rebalanced from a 1,220 base stat total to 600, keeping their shape. Leafipotent: 125/89/125/66/123/72; Vaporipotent: 125/66/123/89/125/72.
Flarichi's pre-evolution is now Flareon (it evolves from Flareon), not Eevee.
Glaceon → Glacida now happens on Snowy Slopes (Roria has no Ice Spikes).
Adds Ash-Mega and Bond-Mega Greninja, each with its own model, alongside the plain Mega: plain Greninja → Mega, Bond → Bond-Mega, Ash → Ash-Mega.

Mega Xerneas and Mega Yveltal added at 780 total stats (Xerneas and Yveltal + 100, like every Mega), made battle-only, Mega Yveltal restored to Dark/Flying (it had lost Dark), and Mega Yveltal now uses its own animations.
Includes the latest Silent's Minemons update: Musheteer is new, 36 learnsets were reworked, and Bognmarrow was removed by the pack.
Erratex, Skelute, Spinerado and Vessilage have no model yet and are hidden until they get one.
Cluckenstein now evolves into Reanderthral (previously a misspelled, missing target), which now has a model.
Bowne no longer evolves into Spinerado (no model yet); Bowne keeps its evolutions into Musheteer, Ivorice and Withereign.
Obese Gourmooze is hidden: it has no art.
Pumpkid → Gallagourd now uses Protective Pads (was an Iron Chestplate).
Mega Talonflame could crash the game because it reused Cobblemon's wing animations for bones its model doesn't have; fixed.

Skull's Mega Expansion 1.0.1: Mega Noivern and Mega Bellibolt, plus Megas for Alolan Raichu, Flygon, Bewear, Centiskorch, Archaludon and Cetitan, each with its own model. Its Flygon and Cetitan Megas sit alongside other packs' Megas on separate slots.
Adds the Slowbronite Mega Stone, which Mega Showdown was missing, so Slowbro (including Galarian Slowbro) can Mega Evolve.
Mega Cryogonal's Pokédex picture framing was corrected.

Snom Betterified restyles Snom and Frosmoth with new models and animations, lets Snom ride on your shoulder, and adds cosmetic items (King's Rock, Silk Scarf, Leather Helmet). The Iron Knife cosmetic was left out (needs Farmer's Delight).
Evolotto had a broken evolution into a non-existent Pokémon ("random"); it was removed.
26 Spaceworldmons that only had a shared placeholder model are hidden from the Pokédex until they get a model.
Spaceworldmons' Gorochu (#1819) was merged away; the Electric/Fire Gorochu at #1729 is the one kept.
Raichu no longer evolves into the removed Spaceworldmons Gorochu.
Each Spaceworldmon now has one form (a duplicate 'Spaceworld' form that looked identical was removed, keeping the real stats), and no Pokémon 'evolves' into itself any more.
Kobat now evolves only into Zubat as intended.

Real form switches (e.g. Twilight forms of Parasect, Pinsir, Tangela, Marowak, Gastrodon, Drifblim and more) are kept, and 13 Spaceworld forms on official Pokémon (Gible, Claydol, Escavalier, Hoppip line, Murkrow, Honchkrow, Marill, Azumarill, Chikorita, Meganium, Girafarig) remain as real alternate forms.
Spaceworldmons' own species (Bomushika, Madamuu and 81 more) showed the default placeholder model in the Pokédex and when spawned by routes or commands. They now show their real models.
Evolotto does not evolve into a random Hoenn Pokémon (Cobblemon has no random evolution); instead you are offered several eligible evolutions to choose from.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Omega.
Ascenshark is no longer labelled restricted.

SpaceworldMons 4.0 renamed its forms to "Beta"; the zones and trainers that used the old name were updated, so Beta Marill, Girafarig, Gible, Basculin, Hoppip, Murkrow and Jumpluff show up as Beta forms again.
Dubfool and Woofloo were shipped by more than one pack; Stellar Blue's versions are the ones kept.
Neuveon was checked against Triple Bakalutions' Nerueon: despite the similar names they are different Eevee variants, and both are kept.
Chirpeck now correctly evolves into Emperoost.

Stellar Blue 1.5 adds 10 species (Aeoleon, Baitin, Coropple, Hummoth, Leefleece, Minursa, Sailin, Spudlett, Spudtrio, Stellysium), a Radiant Eevee form and 10 new moves, and now ships Chirpeck/Emperoost models.
Stellar Blue 1.5 drops Froxicate, Furnauries, Seraphiyon and Amfrosia's Mega (none were available before either).
Eevee → Aeoleon: the held Feather is now used up.
Infastella → Stellotl and Stellumbra: the held Nether Star / Amethyst Shard is now used up.
Coropple → Amfrosia now uses a Syrupy Apple (was an Enchanted Golden Apple).
Pixmini's Pokédex picture framing was corrected.
37 species were wrongly labelled as fossils and no longer are, so they are treated as normal Pokémon in routes (e.g. Asudem, Swimelody, Pixmini, Vegitini, Rooticious, Griffen, Mermadoubt).

Included: 3 new abilities, a new move and retextured Greninja art. Its duplicate Ash-Greninja form was removed, but its art still applies to the official one; Battle Bond and Water Shuriken keep Cobblemon's descriptions.

Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Syn. Eevee, Syn. Espeon, Syn. Flareon, Syn. Glaceon, Syn. Jolteon, Syn. Leafeon, Syn. Sylveon, Syn. Umbreon, Syn. Vaporeon.
Eevee no longer evolves into Syn. Eevee, since it is event-only.
GreenGorilla is now named Green Gorilla.
ThatBoi's Mega Mew keeps the plain "Mega" name; Cusmega's becomes Mega-X.
Layoran Diglett is now a "Layoran" form of Diglett, and Bivouac Colonant a "Bivouac" form of Colonant.
Reginigma was invisible in game ever since its pack was added, due to a broken model file; it now shows.
Lochtrier and Reginigma are now labelled legendary, and Ancient Apparition paradox (kept out of routes).
The New Hisui's Mega Hisuian Diancie is kept as its own Mega alongside the official Mega Diancie.
Hisuian Kakuna was missing from the game (its file clashed with another pack's) and is now back.
Hombone and Hombeast were shipped by more than one pack; Toons Mons' versions are the ones kept.
Infected Caterpie is now an "Infected" form of Caterpie.
Removed a stray copy of Shrufo's evolution from Roscap.
Now Glitch Pokémon (extremely rare in the wild and only found in routes' special Glitch slot): Hombone, Hombeast.
Groudoid, Shriequake, Gasblaster, Biodry, Bioxeny and Bioxenadry are no longer labelled pseudo-legendary, and Spiraleech is no longer labelled secret.
Eevee → Zombeon now uses a Poison Barb (Zombeon is Poison-type). It shared the Reaper Cloth with Phanteon.
Eevee → Phanteon with a Reaper Cloth now actually works; Zombeon's use of the same item meant Phanteon never happened.
The Brick alternatives for evolving Eevee into Phanteon or Zombeon were removed.
Odd Flesh now evolves into Azagorge (both are Dragon/Fire) instead of Cthulon.
Odd Flesh → Azagorge and Mystery Egg → Cthulon now correctly check their level requirement (the field was misspelled).
Nerueon was checked against Stellar Blue's Neuveon: they are different Eevee variants, and both are kept.
Now event-only Pokémon (not found in the wild or in routes, only given out at events): Mikueon, Tetoeon, Nerueon.
Eevee no longer evolves into Mikueon, Tetoeon or Nerueon, since they are event-only.
Twilight Arbok's texture was scrambled because it was painted for Cobblemon's older Arbok model; it now uses a matching model.
Twilight Darmanitan's Zen Mode now shows its art.
Twilight Forest's Transformation Powder is kept as an evolution item.
Its regional variants are now "Regional" forms of the official Pokémon: Joltik, Galvantula, Buneary, Lopunny, Geodude, Ekans, Arbok, Wailmer, Wailord, Dwebble, Doduo, Mareep, Flaaffy and Ampharos.
Basicmon and Herculaias had a broken "???" type: Basicmon is now Normal type and Herculaias is Steel/Ghost.
Mystic Mirage is now Ghost/Psychic. Its original second type (Cosmic) does not exist in the game, and its Cosmic moves were already Psychic-type.
Iron Troupe is now Steel/Normal. Its original second type (Sound) does not exist in the game; as a Meloetta paradox it takes Meloetta's Normal type.
Corkshermit and Dodeca now correctly list the regional Dwebble and regional Doduo as their pre-evolutions (used by the Pokédex and breeding).
Sparking Brute, Iron Troupe, Mystic Mirage and Iron Generator are now labelled paradox Pokémon (kept out of routes).
Yeti Snorlax is now a "Yeti" form of Snorlax.

The pack also carried old copies of Gimmighoul and Gholdengo that quietly changed them (abilities, egg groups, drops, and Gholdengo lost its ability to fly). Those copies were removed, so both are exactly as Cobblemon makes them.
Adds 390 new moves to Pokémon learnsets (none lost), plus custom move effects, 2 abilities and 3 battle conditions.
Kangaskhan's new moves never applied because the pack misspelled its name; that is fixed, so Kangaskhan gets its moves.
Built on ZA Mega 1.8.1. Its copies of Absol Mega-Z, Baxcalibur, Garchomp Mega-Z, Golisopod and Lucario Mega-Z now come from Mega Showdown instead, so there are no duplicate stones. Nothing is lost.
ZA Mega's AZ's Floette ('Ange') was removed because Lost Lore now provides its own; ZA's Ange item can no longer transform Floette and has no recipe.
Not included; the full Big and Small 1.0.1 pack is used instead.

notes.t: Not included; Lots o' Spheal 2.1 is used instead.
Mega Aegislash X and Y were not added: no model at all.
Not added: Mega Showdown already has the same Mega Raichu abilities, and the patch would have removed Mega Raichu X's ability to fly.
Mega Silvally was rejected as too low quality: it replaced all 17 memory forms, had a broken stone, no item icon, a single Normal-type Mega and wasn't battle-only.
The unreleased Mega Skeledirge was not added (renders as a scattered mess and clashes with Mushiro Mega's existing Mega Skeledirge, which stays). Its stone and recipe were removed too.
Mega Victini was not added: the pack has no model at all, so it would look like plain Victini.
Mega Genesect X and Y were not added: no model at all.
Not added: every Gigantamax form it covers (Butterfree, Alcremie) already has a model.
Not added: its Gigantamax forms already have models, and it would have overridden Mega Showdown's Gigantamax models and replaced Inkay and Malamar's normal models.
Removed: its Valentine skins for Bulbasaur, Pikachu and Eevee declared no forms, so they never showed up anywhere.
